root_cause.text: The snapshot creation code treats -EOVERFLOW from btrfs_uuid_tree_add() as a fatal error, causing a transaction abort when repeatedly adding BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL items to the UUID tree exceeds the leaf's item size limit.
root_cause.evidence: The patch comment states: "Fix this by ignoring -EOVERFLOW errors from btrfs_uuid_tree_add() in the snapshot creation code when attempting to add the BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL item." The dmesg shows "insert uuid item failed -75" (-EOVERFLOW) and "BTRFS: Transaction aborted (error -75)". The reproducer demonstrates that snapshotting a received subvolume many times triggers the overflow and forces the filesystem read-only.

This line is part of the function call that can trigger -EOVERFLOW when adding a key of type BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL, which is the specific operation that can overflow the leaf.
This line completes the function call. The objectid parameter is the value being inserted, and repeated insertions cause the -EOVERFLOW error.
This is the conditional that treats any non-zero return value other than -EEXIST as a fatal error. It does not exclude -EOVERFLOW, causing the transaction abort when the leaf size limit is exceeded.
This line aborts the transaction when the condition is true. Since -EOVERFLOW is not excluded, it causes an unnecessary transaction abort, which is the direct effect of the vulnerability.
This line jumps to the fail label after aborting, propagating the error and preventing any recovery from the -EOVERFLOW condition, making the vulnerability fatal.
